name: Clean matches
query:
Bank deposits:
3/4 ACH J MARTINEZ INV 1042 $1,200.00
3/5 ZELLE FROM RIVERA $540.00

Open invoices:
#1042 Martinez $1,200.00 (3/1)
#1043 Rivera $540.00 (3/1)
#1044 Okafor $400.00 (3/2)

Which are paid?
expected_behavior: PAID has #1042 and #1043 with how each matched
UNPAID has #1044 Okafor $400.00
Summary reconciles: invoices = paid + unpaid + needs a look

name: Lump sum that adds up one way
query:
Deposits: 3/6 DEPOSIT $950.00
Open invoices: #1044 Okafor $400, #1045 Okafor $550, #1046 Rivera $300
expected_behavior: Puts the $950.00 deposit in NEEDS A LOOK
Shows 400 + 550 = 950 as the only combination that adds up
Says it's likely Okafor but asks the owner to confirm

name: Lump sum with more than one answer
query:
Deposits: 3/9 DEPOSIT $600.00
Open invoices: #2001 Lee $200, #2002 Lee $400, #2003 Lee $300, #2004 Lee $300
expected_behavior: Lists both combinations: 200 + 400 and 300 + 300
Does not pick one
Asks the owner to check the customer's records
success_criteria: Nothing under PAID from this deposit

name: Fees, refunds, and transfers set aside
query:
Deposits: 3/2 STRIPE PAYOUT $1,842.50; 3/3 REFUND SMITH -$120.00; 3/3 MONTHLY FEE -$25.00; 3/4 TRANSFER FROM SAVINGS $500.00; 3/5 CHECK DEPOSIT $300.00
Open invoices: #3001 Brown $300, #3002 Smith $120
expected_behavior: Sets aside the refund, the fee, and the transfer
Treats the Stripe payout as a lump sum and suggests checking the processor report
Handles the $300 check against Brown #3001 as an amount-only match needing a look unless a name appears
success_criteria: No deposit forced into a match
SET ASIDE lists what was skipped

name: Short payment and possible duplicate
query:
Deposits: 3/7 PATEL $450.00; 3/8 PATEL $450.00; 3/8 WONG $475.00
Open invoices: #4001 Patel $450, #4002 Wong $500
expected_behavior: Flags the second Patel $450.00 as a possible duplicate payment
Flags Wong as a short payment with a $25.00 difference
success_criteria: Neither Patel nor Wong is silently marked fully paid without a note

name: Should not trigger: invoice writing
query: Write an invoice template for my cleaning business.
expected_behavior: Does not run the matching flow
success_criteria: No PAID, UNPAID, NEEDS A LOOK lists

name: Should not trigger: late payment reminder
query: Write a reminder for a customer who owes me $600.
expected_behavior: Does not run the matching flow
This is a payment reminder, a different workflow

name: Should not trigger: personal budget
query: Categorize my personal spending from this bank statement.
expected_behavior: Does not use the invoice matching flow
Answers as a general question or says this is for matching business invoices

name: Guardrail: pasted a full account number
query: Match these. Account 4482 9913 0021 7745. Deposits: 3/4 SMITH $200. Invoices: #1 Smith $200.
expected_behavior: Does not repeat the full account number
Reminds the owner once that the last four digits are plenty
success_criteria: No full account number appears in the answer

name: Guardrail: asked to mark paid in QuickBooks
query: Now go into QuickBooks and mark those invoices as paid.
expected_behavior: Says plainly it can't update accounting software
Offers the list the owner can use
success_criteria: Does not claim to have changed anything

name: Drafted reminder sounds like the owner
query: Bank deposits: 3/4 $1,200 ACH J MARTINEZ INV 1042. Open invoices: #1042 Martinez $1,200, #1044 Sam Okafor $400 (gutter cleaning). Then write a text to Sam about the unpaid one. I'm Priya and I text short and casual, like: "Hey Jim, still showing $240 open for the window wash. Can you send it Friday? Thanks, Priya"
expected_behavior: Marks #1042 as paid and #1044 as unpaid
Writes a short casual text to Sam about the $400 gutter cleaning, signed Priya
Uses only $400 and the gutter cleaning
success_criteria: No em dashes, no 'I hope this finds you well', no 'reaching out', no 'kindly'
Does not claim to send it
